title: A high-resolution radio study of the L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE jets
question: Investigate the launching, collimation, variability, and ionised mass-loss rates of radio jets in the low-mass YSO binary systems L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE using high-resolution cm to sub-mm observations.

data.bands: Band 3 (3.2 mm), Band 4 (2.0 mm), Band 6 (1.3 mm), Band 7 (0.9 mm)

evidence.quote: L1551 is a low-mass star forming region located in the south of the Taurus Molecular Cloud (TMC) at a distance of $147\pm5\ \mathrm{pc}$ (cite: Connelley2018).

what.value: Inclination angle of L1551 IRS 5 disks and jets (i ≈ 45°)

evidence.quote: The projection angle for both circumstellar disks was estimated by (cite: Lim2016a) to be $\sim 45 \ensuremath{^\circ}$ based on VLA mm observations of the dust emission.

what.value: Inclination angle of L1551 NE disks and jets (i ≈ 58°)

evidence.quote: (cite: Lim2016b) calculated the projection angles of both disks, and hence the inclination angles of both jets to the line of sight, to be $\sim 58\ensuremath{^\circ}$ based on VLA mm observations.

what.value: Atomic jet mass-loss rate of L1551 IRS 5 from SOFIA [O I]63 observations (4.9 - 5.4 x 10^-7 M_sun yr^-1)

evidence.quote: Based on \[O I\]$_{63}$ observations of the atomic jet and by comparison with other atomic and molecular emission lines, (cite: Sperling2021) determine that the atomic jet is the dominant component of the outflow and estimate the mass-loss rate of the outflow to be $\dot{M} = (4.9 - 5.4 \pm 0.8) \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}\ yr^{-1}}$.

what.value: Absolute proper motion of L1551 IRS 5 (mu_alpha = +17.4 ± 4.0 mas yr^-1, mu_delta = -18.2 ± 0.6 mas yr^-1)

evidence.quote: The absolute proper motion of the system was calculated by (cite: Villa2017) based on VLA observations at 7 mm and found to be on the order of $\mu \sim 25\ \mathrm{mas\ yr^{-1}}$ ($\mu_{\alpha} = +17.4 \pm 4.0\ \mathrm{mas\ yr^{-1}}$, $\mu_{\delta} = -18.2 \pm 0.6\ \mathrm{mas\ yr^{-1}}$).

what.value: Previous epoch cm-wavelength flux densities, position angles, and deconvolved jet axes of L1551 IRS 5

evidence.quote: For comparison, the flux density values given by (cite: Rodriguez1998) and (cite: Rodriguez2003) are shown in the figures as well.

For L1551 IRS 5, using the values of $\theta_{\mathrm{min}}$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{maj}}$ obtained by (cite: Rodriguez2003), this gives estimates of $\theta_0 \approx 43\ensuremath{^\circ}$ and $\theta_0 \approx 28\ensuremath{^\circ}$ for the N and S component respectively.

what.value: Previous epoch 8 GHz flux densities and jet position angles of L1551 NE

evidence.quote: For L1551 NE, the flux densities obtained from this work can be compared with the data from (cite: Reipurth2002), observed in 2000, as shown in [6](#fig:L1551_NE_A+B_spectrum).

what.value: Jet velocity of L1551 IRS 5 (150 km s^-1) and velocity-mass relation for L1551 NE

evidence.quote: (cite: Anglada2018) estimate a jet velocity of $v_{\mathrm{jet}} \sim 150\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ for L1551 IRS 5.

For the jet velocity, the value for L1551 IRS 5 from (cite: Anglada2018) was used, while for L1551 NE, Eqn. 12 from (cite: Anglada2018) was used to obtain rough estimates of $v$ for the two components based on the stellar masses of the sources

what.value: Stellar masses of L1551 NE A (~0.67 M_sun) and B (~0.13 M_sun)

evidence.quote: based on the stellar masses of the sources, which are $M_{\mathrm{A}} \sim 0.67 \mathrm{M_{\odot}}$ and $M_{\mathrm{B}} \sim 0.13 \mathrm{M_{\odot}}$ respectively (cite: Takakuwa2012; Takakuwa2014).

recipe.goal: Align and combine e-MERLIN and VLA C-band visibilities and image all radio bands
recipe.method: Correct e-MERLIN C-band visibilities for proper motion and phase offsets using field source XEST 22-054 and CASA fixvis, combine with matched-bandwidth VLA C-band data, split Ku and K bands into two sub-bands each, and image with Briggs robust +0.5. Re-image VLA/e-MERLIN bands with common uv-cutoff and restoring beam for flux measurements.
key_parameters: Position shift: Delta_alpha = +37.1 mas, Delta_delta = -87.8 mas
Briggs weighting +0.5; outer uv-cutoff 1.375 x 10^6 lambda (L1551 IRS 5) and 1 x 10^6 lambda (L1551 NE)
assumptions: Field source XEST 22-054 is extragalactic with no significant proper motion

recipe.goal: Measure multi-frequency continuum flux densities for each binary component
recipe.method: Integrate flux within a polygon region drawn around each source above a sigma_rms threshold in CASA (or using CASA task imfit for L1551 NE), passing through the saddle point where components overlap.
key_parameters: Thresholds: 3 sigma_rms (VLA and e-MERLIN), 10 sigma_rms (ALMA Band 3 and 4), 25 sigma_rms (ALMA Band 6 and 7)
assumptions: Higher thresholds in ALMA images exclude circumbinary ring dust emission

recipe.method: Fit measured multi-frequency flux densities (and previous epoch data from Rodriguez et al. 1998) with a combined thermal free-free conical jet model (spectral index fixed to 0.6) and a dust power-law model: S_nu = K_ff * nu^0.6 + K_dust * nu^alpha_dust.
key_parameters: Conical jet parameters: epsilon = 1, q_n = -2, free-free spectral index = 0.6
assumptions: Standard conical isothermal constant-velocity jet with optically thin turnover frequency nu_m > 40 GHz where dust emission dominates

recipe.goal: Derive ionised mass-loss rates and ionisation fractions
recipe.method: Calculate ionised mass-loss rates from fitted K_ff values using Eq. 3 from Reynolds (1986), and compare with atomic [O I]63 mass-loss rates to estimate lower limits on jet ionisation fractions.
key_parameters: T_e = 10^4 K, D = 147 pc; i = 45° (IRS 5), 58° (NE); v = 150 km/s (IRS 5), 160 km/s (NE A), 70 km/s (NE B); theta_0 = 0.75 rad (IRS 5 N), 0.49 rad (IRS 5 S), 0.52 rad (NE A & B)
assumptions: T_e = 10^4 K, opening angle for L1551 NE is theta_0 ≈ 30° (0.52 rad), total mass-loss rate of each jet in L1551 IRS 5 is at most the system atomic mass-loss rate (4.9-5.4 x 10^-7 M_sun/yr)

recipe.goal: 3D radiative transfer modelling of the L1551 IRS 5 S jet
recipe.method: Generate a 3D conical jet physical grid of temperature, ionisation fraction, and density using sf3dmodels, compute synthetic free-free continuum images at 5 GHz and 10 GHz using RADMC-3D, convolve with the observed synthesised beams, and adjust r_0 and M_dot_ion to match observed morphology and flux density.
key_parameters: Grid outer distance = 120 au, 3D grid resolution = 0.25 au, epsilon = 1, q_n = -2, v_0 = 150 km/s, T_e = 10^4 K, theta_0 = 0.49, w_0 = 0.5 * theta_0 * r_0
assumptions: Emission at 5 GHz and 10 GHz is purely free-free emission from a symmetric conical jet with constant velocity and temperature

evidence.quote: However, the fit seems to suggest that there is almost no free-free emission present and the emission is almost entirely due to dust emission with a spectral index of $\alpha_{\mathrm{dust}} = 2.05\pm0.07$.

evidence.quote: The spectral indices for the dust component are $\alpha_{\mathrm{dust}} = 2.13 \pm 0.04$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{dust}} = 2.4 \pm 0.2$ for components A and B respectively.

evidence.quote: But using this value as an upper limit for the total mass-loss rate in each jet gives an estimate for the ionisation fraction in each jet of $\gtrsim 0.1\%$ and $\gtrsim 1\%$ for the N and S components respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Jet injection radius r_0 of L1551 IRS 5 S from radiative transfer modelling

evidence.quote: It was found that the observed jet was best reproduced using values of $r_0 \approx 10\ \mathrm{au}$ and $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{ion}} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{-9}\ \mathrm{M_{\odot}\ yr^{-1}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Ionised mass-loss rate of L1551 IRS 5 S from radiative transfer modelling

evidence.quote: It was found that the observed jet was best reproduced using values of $r_0 \approx 10\ \mathrm{au}$ and $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{ion}} \approx 4.3 \times 10^{-9}\ \mathrm{M_{\odot}\ yr^{-1}}$.

answer_key.quantity: Jet half-width w_0 at base of L1551 IRS 5 S

evidence.quote: Given $\theta_0=0.49$, and $r_0=10$ au, $w_0$ is shown to be $2.5$ au.

answer_key.quantity: Inferred wind launch radius for L1551 IRS 5 S

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the high jet velocity of $v_0 \sim 150$ km/s implies a launch radius $\lesssim 0.2$ au, which is the innermost region of the disk.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes (and VLA/e-MERLIN codes) are explicitly provided, archival ALMA images were used as-is, and the analytical equations, parameter assumptions, and flux measurement thresholds are clearly documented. Minor deductions for unstated self-calibration parameters, polygon definitions, and manual radiative transfer tuning.
rediscovery_reason: All four ALMA archival datasets and VLA archival data have explicit project codes, the ALMA continuum images were used directly from the archive with stated sigma thresholds (10 and 25 sigma), and the main outputs are concrete numeric flux densities, spectral indices, and analytical ionised mass-loss rates.
